markdown_report:
At 10% progress, prioritize a small **directional recent-history residual**, conditional on establishing a matched objective baseline. Earlier residual attempts scored 0.4037–0.4100 versus the supplied SASRec reference of 0.5050; without matched configurations, these results discourage optimism but do not identify the cause.

**Insights and directions.** First, zero initialization preserves initial scores, not subsequent optimization. This supports controlled residual experiments. Second, recurrence can emphasize narrow interests but suppress emerging ones. Defer recurrence gating. Third, Electronics’ 15.96% sampled negative-win rate motivates separation experiments without identifying their cause.

Related work supplies three further insights. SASRec already produces directional, history-dependent predictions despite tied embeddings [1]. FPMC/FOSSIL establish asymmetric transitions and pooled recent histories, reducing novelty [2]. gSASRec motivates negative-count/calibration studies, while candidate CE is a separate intervention [3,4]. These organize context selection, relation parameterization, and objective calibration.

| Framework axis | Existing mechanism | Proposed experiment | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Context | SASRec; FOSSIL history pooling | Three-event exponential pooling | Recency does not establish purpose |
| Relations | FPMC/FOSSIL directed factors | Zero-start bilinear residual | Direction does not establish compatibility |
| Competition | Original BCE; multi-negative BCE; CE | Matched sampler/objective controls | Sampled margins differ from validation HR@10 |

**Candidate assessment.** Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each dimension has a positive and negative reason.

| Idea | Scores | Positive / negative assessment by dimension |
|---|---|---|
| A. Directional recent residual | 2/6/6/6/4 | O: specific SASRec extension / strong prior art; P: extensible / sparse transitions; U: recent successors / usefulness unverified; M: separation / cause uncertain; D: small module / matched controls |
| B. Recency–recurrence gate | 3/6/7/5/5 | O: causal support / familiar gating; P: adaptive evidence / interest lock-in; U: narrow recurrence / new interests suppressed; M: context filtering / sensitivity unmeasured; D: backbone retained / masking complexity |
| C. Matched-negative gBCE | 2/6/3/8/3 | O: controlled transfer / established loss; P: calibration / CE advantage unknown; U: fewer distractors / no intent mechanism; M: competition / sampled proxy; D: local change / sampling cost |

**Selected: A.** Explicit user-facing targets are broad relatedness displacing recent narrow interests and past artist/device-family interactions implying continuing demand for related variants. Recent ordered-successor supervision tests both hypotheses; it cannot identify satisfied demand, compatibility, or replacement need. Its model-facing target is sampled positive–negative inversion, especially Electronics.

Use causal pooling and separate source/target projections with a zero-start coefficient. Establish original BCE, matched multi-negative BCE, and matched CE references before attributing gains to architecture. Compare full bilinear and parameter-matched symmetric residuals; defer additional gates. Training-only skew-score and popularity-matched transition probes assess shortcuts, not relevance. Preserve routing, splits, seeds, interfaces, and shared budget; select only by pinned macro validation HR@10. Repeated validation selection remains exploratory. No gain is claimed.

References: [1] [SASRec](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.09781); [2] [FOSSIL/FPMC](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.09152); [3] [gSASRec](https://www.ijcai.org/proceedings/2024/0939.pdf); [4] [CE implementation](https://github.com/antklen/sasrec-bert4rec-recsys23).

idea.description: Add a zero-initialized directional recent-history scoring residual to each category-specific RecHarness SASRec: score(t,i) = h_t^T E_i + alpha (A r_t)^T(B E_i), where r_t pools the latest three causal raw item embeddings with weights 1, 0.5, 0.25, excluding padding and renormalizing. A and B are independent, bias-free d-by-d projections initialized to identity; alpha starts at zero. Do not implement this by multiplying augmented backbone and candidate vectors, which introduces unintended cross terms. SASRec already models directed predictions; the hypothesis concerns the incremental benefit of an explicit recent bilinear path. Candidate-set CE is an experimental objective, not the original RecHarness SASRec loss. Establish matched objective references before assessing this architecture.
idea.motivation: The two explicit user-facing targets are broad relatedness crowding out recent narrow interests and past interactions with an artist, device family, or product type being interpreted as continuing demand for related variants. Recency weighting emphasizes immediate evidence; ordered successor supervision may downrank related variants that do not commonly follow that evidence. Both are hypotheses, and the model cannot identify actual ownership, fulfilled demand, replacement need, compatibility, dimensions, quantity, or mood. The model-facing target is positive–negative ranking inversion: Electronics has a 0.1596 sampled negative-win rate and a −0.4829 tenth-percentile margin; Industrial_and_Scientific also has a negative lower-tail margin. Sampled margins depend on the sampler and score scale and do not establish validation quality. Earlier residual scores below the supplied reference motivate stronger controls rather than a claim that residuals or asymmetry will help.
idea.implementation_notes:
Preserve four independently trained category models and routing for Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, and CDs_and_Vinyl. Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, unchanged input splits, trial-local artifacts, single-GPU execution, and SASREC_EPOCHS with the supplied environment default of 200. Use only public training histories, timestamps, titles, and descriptions. This experiment requires histories alone. Reviews, ratings, item category labels, prices, stores, ownership, and simulator diversity/conformity traits remain unavailable; generic example schemas do not authorize their use.

Architecture: retain baseline dimensions, encoder, final normalization, masking, and raw tied item embeddings. Pool positions t, t−1, t−2 with weights 1, 0.5, 0.25 and padding-aware renormalization. No positional embeddings or encoder sqrt(d) multiplier enter this branch. Pooling uses positions within the original sequence, without consulting later items. Return zero for empty windows and padded queries. Add no normalization after the score residual. Construct baseline modules and perform their initialization first. Construct A and B afterward inside a separate RNG context that restores CPU and applicable CUDA RNG states; initialize both to identity and alpha exactly to zero. Initial equality requires identical baseline weights, finite branch outputs, and matched stochastic state. A and B receive zero residual gradients initially; alpha can learn immediately. Once alpha changes, independent A and B can learn asymmetry. Zero initialization does not ensure later stability.

Optimizer: preserve every baseline parameter group and resolved optimizer setting. Add A and B in an explicit group using the baseline learning rate, betas, epsilon, and the existing policy for comparable projection weights; log its weight decay. Put alpha in a separate group with the same optimizer settings and zero weight decay. Keep update counts, batch size, encoder dimensions, regularization, validation opportunities, and checkpoint rules matched across comparisons. Explicitly document any mismatch forced by the GPU budget. Preserving RNG state prevents branch construction from changing initial training randomness; it does not make later stochastic trajectories identical across different objectives.

Objective/sampler contract for new multi-negative arms: K=256, temperature=1.0. At each valid timestep independently sample a uniform subset without replacement from the category catalog excluding padding and that user's COMPLETE training-positive set. Never consult held-out labels. Resample on each presentation; do not share sampled sets across timesteps. If fewer than K items are eligible, use all eligible items and mask unused slots. Log eligible-pool shortages; this contract requires user identity or a precomputed per-example exclusion handle internally. Preserve the diagnostic loader's (None, sequence, positive, negative) interface through a separate adapter; do not attempt to reconstruct complete user histories from truncated sequences. Rows with no eligible negatives contribute zero to the specified objective and should be counted separately. Skip batches with no valid targets. Use chunked scoring if needed; do not allocate a full B×L×K×d tensor. Candidate CE is -s_positive + logsumexp([s_positive, eligible negative scores]), summed over positive!=0 positions and divided by their count. Do not divide CE by K or average over padded B×L positions. Multi-negative BCE is softplus(-s_positive) + mean_j softplus(s_negative_j), averaged over valid targets; define the zero-negative row contribution as zero to match its uninformative candidate CE counterpart and report its frequency. These are proposed reproducibility choices, not SASRec/gSASRec defaults. Original reference training remains unchanged, including its own sampler and normalization.

Experimental sequence: R0 unchanged RecHarness SASRec+BCE; R1 plain SASRec+multi-negative BCE with the specified sampler; R2 plain SASRec+candidate CE with that same sampler; R3 full residual+CE. R0 versus R1 measures the combined negative-count/sampler change, not negative count alone if eligibility differs. R1 versus R2 isolates the defined objective change. R2 versus R3 isolates the residual under CE. Residual+BCE completes the interaction check if budget permits; do not claim objective-independent gains without it. Match updates and validation opportunities while reporting actual GPU consumption, since equal updates and equal runtime are different comparisons. Run arms sequentially in priority order within the externally supplied remaining budget; these arms are not an instruction to exceed it.

Asymmetry control: for column-vector embeddings, M=A^T B and residual=r^T M e. The previous shared-projection control A^T A is positive semidefinite and halves projection parameters, confounding symmetry with capacity and spectral constraints. Instead retrain a control with score alpha/2*((A r)^T(B e)+(B r)^T(A e)), using the same A,B dimensions, identity initialization, parameter count, optimizer policy, and validation opportunities. This implements S=(M+M^T)/2. Report effective matrix ranks: symmetric controls can have different rank capacity for low-rank factors, although d-by-d factors here both have rank at most d. At full rank this symmetric parameterization permits indefinite matrices. Skew-only retraining and a parameter-matched signed-Gram control C^T J C are deferred, budget-dependent extensions. Supplement retraining by removing K=(M−M^T)/2 from the trained full model; this ablation is descriptive and does not replace a retrained control. Directional novelty must be assessed against FPMC/FOSSIL, not just tied similarity. TiCoSeRec supplies additional directed-transition motivation, not evidence for this specific residual.

Diagnostics: preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions. view.model must be the actual trained nn.Module; view.item_emb remains the shared E table. log2feats returns concatenated scoring features, and predict_score uses matching candidate representations. Adapt every scoring probe to call predict_score rather than assuming feature and embedding dimensions coincide. Preserve user_train, meta_data, and review_data interfaces without fabricating missing fields. Keep train_loader outputs (None, sequence, positive, negative), each tensor B×L. Use a separate fixed diagnostic sample or loader; do not consume or perturb the live training iterator. Preserve existing sampled-margin definitions and the embedding-alignment definition; alignment measures E only and is not proof of collapse. Supplementary probes require explicit shared remaining-budget accounting; unavailable probes remain unavailable.

On a fixed training-only sample, monitor alpha, feature norms, absolute residual/base score magnitudes, candidate-score differences, and unchanged sampled negative-win rates. For M=S+K, report actual |alpha*r^T K e|, symmetric contributions, and total residual contributions; parameter norms alone do not establish useful asymmetry. For single-item sources, compare forward-minus-reverse scores, excluding biases, with training transition-count asymmetry. Compare genuine transitions with reversed pairs and frequency-matched nontransitions using identical fixed candidates; stratify by source/target frequency and transition support. These diagnose popularity and first-order shortcuts, not higher-order reasoning or practical usefulness. Optional perturbations include earlier-item shuffling preserving the last item, swapping the last two, dropping recent items, and frequency/similarity-matched last-item replacement. Pooling is order-sensitive only through unequal lag weights; do not claim that any shuffle necessarily changes its output. Perturbed histories may be implausible. Popularity-only, last-item similarity, and first-order transition baselines are descriptive training probes, not additional selection metrics.

For the twenty designated real training users, retain full-catalog unseen-item recommendations, five users per category, excluding all observed training items. Separately report coverage, recommendation popularity, concentration, and recent-history similarity when budget permits. These statistics do not establish relevance, user conformity, or simulator preference traits. Sampled validation and full-catalog diagnostics can disagree; only the pinned host macro validation HR@10 selects models.

Budget/selection: subtract all previous consumption from the shared 43,200 GPU-second allowance before scheduling. The host must charge actual single-GPU time for training, checkpoint inspections, diagnostics, debugging, and failures across all slots; local elapsed-time limits alone cannot enforce the shared balance. Preserve and record the baseline validation cadence and checkpoint policy. Compare category models at the same declared configuration/checkpoint opportunity and select their bundle by host-provided four-category macro validation HR@10; do not independently choose category checkpoints unless a separately declared validation search permits and accounts for that additional flexibility. Ties favor earlier checkpoints, then the simpler configuration. Do not recreate or modify host candidates, access hidden tests, or fabricate unavailable outcomes. Retain per-category scores and all attempted configurations when exposed. Optional paired user-bootstrap intervals require host-provided paired hits and describe uncertainty conditional on fixed models/candidates, not seed stability or selection-corrected significance. Repeated validation inspection can overfit 800 fixed users, so restrict the declared search and treat gains as exploratory. Final held-out inference remains the separate host step.

Serialization: update the predictor writer with identical architecture, pooling weights, scoring mode, dimensions, alpha, A/B parameters, mappings, and category routing. Store resolved sampler/objective settings and optimizer configuration with each trial. Before training, verify finite empty-window handling, zero-alpha valid-position baseline-score equality, suffix invariance of earlier scores, a finite nonzero alpha gradient on a nondegenerate example, and checkpoint-reload score equality. Test all supported candidate layouts explicitly. No such verification or training has been executed in this report. Potential shortcut learning includes head-item preference, local co-occurrence, symmetric similarity, and repeated-interest lock-in; the proposed controls constrain the claims rather than eliminating these risks.
idea.pseudocode:
import torch
from torch import nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

class DirectionalRecentResidual(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, dim, symmetric=False):
        super().__init__()
        self.source = nn.Linear(dim, dim, bias=False)
        self.target = nn.Linear(dim, dim, bias=False)
        nn.init.eye_(self.source.weight)
        nn.init.eye_(self.target.weight)
        self.alpha = nn.Parameter(torch.zeros(()))
        self.symmetric = bool(symmetric)

    def features(self, baseline_features, sequence, item_emb):
        valid = sequence.ne(0)
        emb = item_emb(sequence).masked_fill(~valid.unsqueeze(-1), 0)
        # Float32 pooling avoids small-denominator underflow with mixed precision.
        values = emb.float()
        pooled = torch.zeros_like(values)
        count = values.new_zeros(sequence.shape)
        for lag, weight in enumerate((1.0, 0.5, 0.25)):
            if lag >= sequence.size(1):
                break
            if lag == 0:
                shifted_emb, shifted_valid = values, valid
            else:
                shifted_emb = F.pad(values[:, :-lag], (0, 0, lag, 0))
                shifted_valid = F.pad(valid[:, :-lag], (lag, 0))
            pooled = pooled + weight * shifted_emb
            count = count + weight * shifted_valid.float()
        pooled = (pooled / count.clamp_min(1e-8).unsqueeze(-1)).to(emb.dtype)
        if self.symmetric:
            parts = (baseline_features,
                     0.5 * self.alpha * self.source(pooled),
                     0.5 * self.alpha * self.target(pooled))
        else:
            parts = (baseline_features, self.alpha * self.source(pooled))
        return torch.cat(parts, dim=-1).masked_fill(~valid.unsqueeze(-1), 0)

    def candidates(self, item_ids, item_emb):
        e = item_emb(item_ids)
        if self.symmetric:
            return torch.cat((e, self.target(e), self.source(e)), dim=-1)
        return torch.cat((e, self.target(e)), dim=-1)

    def score_aligned(self, features, item_ids, item_emb):
        # features: (..., D); item_ids: matching (...).
        return (features * self.candidates(item_ids, item_emb)).sum(-1)

    def score_per_position(self, features, item_ids, item_emb):
        # features: (..., D); item_ids: (..., K).
        return (features.unsqueeze(-2) * self.candidates(item_ids, item_emb)).sum(-1)

    def score_shared_catalog(self, features, item_ids, item_emb):
        # features: (..., D); item_ids: (C,). Call with catalog chunks.
        return features @ self.candidates(item_ids, item_emb).transpose(-1, -2)

# Construct baseline and complete its unchanged initialization first.
# Create the residual within torch.random.fork_rng(devices=applicable_cuda_indices)
# so nn.Linear initialization does not advance the baseline training RNG stream.
# The actual SASRec.log2feats returns residual.features(original_h, sequence, item_emb).
# Actual model.predict_score dispatches EXPLICITLY by documented candidate layout;
# never infer ambiguous layouts solely from tensor rank.

# Multi-negative training contract; host data pipeline supplies complete training
# exclusion sets through internal user handles, independent of diagnostic tuples.
for batch in training_batches:
    sequence, positive, user_handles = batch
    valid = positive.ne(0)
    if not valid.any():
        continue
    features = model.log2feats(sequence)[valid]
    targets = positive[valid]
    # Independently resample each row, uniformly WITHOUT replacement.
    # Exclude 0 and COMPLETE training positives; use all eligible if fewer than 256.
    negatives, neg_mask = sample_uniform_training_complement(
        user_handles, valid, K=256, share_across_timesteps=False)
    pos_score = model.predict_score(features, targets, layout='aligned')
    neg_score = score_negative_chunks(model, features, negatives)
    has_negative = neg_mask.any(-1)
    if objective == 'candidate_ce':
        masked_neg = neg_score.masked_fill(~neg_mask, -torch.inf)
        logits = torch.cat((pos_score[:, None], masked_neg), dim=-1) / 1.0
        per_row = F.cross_entropy(
            logits, torch.zeros_like(targets, dtype=torch.long), reduction='none')
    elif objective == 'multi_negative_bce':
        neg_term = F.softplus(neg_score).masked_fill(~neg_mask, 0).sum(-1)
        neg_term = neg_term / neg_mask.sum(-1).clamp_min(1)
        per_row = F.softplus(-pos_score) + neg_term
        per_row = per_row.masked_fill(~has_negative, 0)
    loss = per_row.sum() / valid.sum()
    # Count zero-negative rows; skip optimizer update if every row has zero loss.
    if has_negative.any():
        optimizer.zero_grad(set_to_none=True)
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()

# R0 uses the UNCHANGED RecHarness baseline training path, not this new sampler.
# R1: plain + specified multi-negative BCE. R2: plain + specified CE.
# R3: full residual + CE. Next: parameter-matched symmetric residual + CE.
# Residual+BCE and skew-only retraining are conditional on remaining shared budget.
# Serialize scoring mode and all parameters into checkpoints and predictor writer.
# Select bundles solely by host-provided four-category macro validation HR@10.

originality.positive: The specific zero-start SASRec residual and controlled decomposition provide a clear, falsifiable incremental experiment.
originality.negative: FPMC and FOSSIL already combine asymmetric transition factors with preference or recent-history signals; SASRec itself already supports directional predictions.

future_potential.positive: Matched objective and bilinear controls could reveal whether a cheap explicit recent path adds value and justify later context-dependent transitions or calibration studies.
future_potential.negative: Earlier residual attempts underperformed the supplied reference, sparse transitions encourage shortcuts, and the available observations cannot identify satisfied demand or practical compatibility.

code_difficulty.positive: The model extension uses two small projections, one scalar, short-window pooling, and no graph construction or external data.
code_difficulty.negative: Complete-history negative exclusions, chunked multi-negative scoring, parameter-matched controls, diagnostic layouts, predictor generation, and shared-budget accounting exceed the complexity of the module alone.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides the causal self-attention backbone and next-item scoring baseline.
History-dependent nonlinear features and positional information permit directional predictions despite tied item embeddings.
Original implementation uses sampled BCE; the unchanged RecHarness implementation remains the experimental reference.
limitations: Does not establish ownership, compatibility, or immediate practical demand from interaction histories.
Adding an explicit directed residual must demonstrate benefit beyond the backbone's existing temporal capacity.

related_work.title: FOSSIL: Factored Similarity Models with High-Order Markov Chains
contributions: Combines a history aggregate and weighted recent-item representations scored against separate target embeddings.
Discusses FPMC's combination of user–item preferences and asymmetric item-transition factors.
Provides direct prior art for the proposed recent asymmetric residual and limits its novelty.
limitations: Does not establish incremental benefits when this mechanism is added to SASRec under the pinned benchmark.
Observed successor associations do not identify complementarity, replacement need, or causal demand.

related_work.title: TiCoSeRec
contributions: The supplied search summary describes weighted directed transition information integrated into sequential recommendation.
Motivates testing ordered behavioral information as an additional signal.
limitations: Its graph-based mechanism differs from the proposed lightweight bilinear residual.
Reported results do not establish gains under this RecHarness protocol.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Motivates increasing negative counts and generalized BCE calibration.
The supplied official-repository summary recommends K=256 and calibration t=0.75 as a possible separate experiment.
limitations: Generalized BCE is distinct from candidate-set CE and does not define its temperature or normalization.
Evidence against BCE does not establish superiority over matched candidate CE.
Objective calibration alone supplies no explicit mechanism for recent intent or useful successors.

related_work.title: Authors' SASRec/BERT4Rec implementation with categorical cross-entropy
contributions: Provides precedent for categorical cross-entropy training of SASRec.
Supports treating CE as an established objective intervention requiring explicit sampling and normalization.
limitations: Implementation precedent does not establish that the proposed K=256 sampler improves this task.
Objective and negative-sampling changes require separate attribution.

related_work.title: Sequential-recommendation dataset and order-sensitivity analysis
contributions: The supplied search summary motivates order-breaking controls because accuracy can persist after shuffling.
Supports distinguishing directional capacity from demonstrated use of temporal structure.
limitations: Perturbed histories may be implausible and are not causal preference interventions.
Order sensitivity does not establish relevance or higher-order reasoning.

related_work.title: On the Bias of Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Motivates distinguishing sampled-candidate evaluation from full-catalog recommendation behavior.
limitations: Does not justify replacing the pinned evaluator or selecting models with supplementary full-catalog diagnostics.
Does not predict which proposed model will improve the fixed macro validation HR@10.
